name: Off-Road Recreational Vehicle
description: Includes any two-wheeled motorcycle not required to be licensed that weighs 600 pounds or less and is designed to be ridden off-road astride a seat, such as an electric dirt bike like a Sur-Ron or Talaria.

restrictions.rule: Two tires, a seat or saddle ridden astride, designed for off-road riding, unladen weight of 600 pounds or less, and not required to be licensed; no limit on motor power or speed
Not a motorcycle for registration purposes
Needs an annual Wyoming off-road recreational vehicle trail user decal ($15) from the Department of State Parks and Cultural Resources to ride designated ORV trails
Allowed on a public road only where the road is designated open and marked as a Wyoming ORV trail, with proof of liability insurance of at least $25,000 and a valid driver's license or permit

May be registered and plated for road use, at the motorcycle rate, if titled in Wyoming, used mainly for off-road recreation, and certified to have the required lights, horn, mirror and muffler; it may then use any open public road
Needs adequate brakes, a horn, muffler and mirror on public roads, lights from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, and a spark arrester on state or federal land

Never allowed on an interstate roadway or right-of-way, except as department rules allow, or on a marked Wyoming ORV trail beside it behind a physical barrier or crossing over or under it, with a valid driver's license and a plate or ORV decal
Riders and passengers under 18 must wear a helmet when it's ridden on a public road for farm work, which needs a motorcycle-endorsed license
